knowledge:
- key_parameters: binary_truth=The column name in the truth data frame representing the true binary classification status (e.g., "status") ;; cont_truth=The column name in the truth data frame representing the true continuous score (e.g., "logFC") ;; splv=The stratification variable name from the truth data frame (e.g., "expr_cat" or "none") ;; maxsplit=The maximum number of categories to retain when stratifying (default is 4) ;; colorscheme=A pre-defined color palette name (e.g., "Dark2") or a character vector of custom colors ;; facetted=A logical indicating whether plotting should be split into panels based on the stratification variable
- alternatives: limma::vennDiagram=Used internally by plot_overlap to generate Venn diagrams, and accepts additional arguments like cex to customize text size
- when_to_use: When evaluating and comparing the performance of multiple ranking or binary classification methods (e.g., comparing differential expression tools like edgeR, DESeq2, and voom) against a known ground truth.
- pitfalls: Stratifying by continuous annotations is not supported because each category would likely contain only one observation; only categorical/discrete variables should be used for splv ;; If the wrong number of colors is provided in colorscheme, iCOBRA will automatically add or remove colors ;; Methods without adjusted p-values must have them calculated using calculate_adjp before certain performance metrics can be computed.

workflows.name: performance_evaluation_and_plotting
workflows.intent: Programmatically calculate and plot performance metrics (TPR, FDR, ROC, overlap) for ranking and binary classification methods.
input: Data frames containing p-values, adjusted p-values, scores, and ground truth (binary status and/or continuous scores) for features.
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package and example data (or user data formatted as a COBRAData object) ;; 2. Calculate adjusted p-values if missing using calculate_adjp ;; 3. Calculate performance metrics using calculate_performance ;; 4. Prepare data for plotting using prepare_data_for_plot ;; 5. Generate performance plots using plot_tpr, plot_fdrtprcurve, and plot_overlap.
workflows.code:
library(iCOBRA)
data(cobradata_example)
class(cobradata_example)
cobradata_example
cobradata_example <- calculate_adjp(cobradata_example)
cobraperf <- calculate_performance(cobradata_example, binary_truth = "status", 
                                  cont_truth = "logFC", splv = "none",
                                  maxsplit = 4)
slotNames(cobraperf)
cobraplot <- prepare_data_for_plot(cobraperf, colorscheme = "Dark2", 
                                  facetted = TRUE)
plot_tpr(cobraplot)
plot_fdrtprcurve(cobraplot)
plot_overlap(cobraplot)

workflows.name: interactive_shiny_visualization
workflows.intent: Launch the interactive Shiny application to explore performance metrics.
input: A COBRAData object or text files containing truth and results.
workflows.stages: 1. Launch the Shiny app using COBRAapp.

workflows.name: text_file_import_export
workflows.intent: Convert between COBRAData objects and text files for external storage or app compatibility.
input: A COBRAData object or text files containing truth and results.
workflows.stages: 1. Export COBRAData to text files using COBRAData_to_text ;; 2. Import text files back into a COBRAData object using COBRAData_from_text.
workflows.code:
COBRAData_to_text(cobradata = cobradata_example, 
                  truth_file = "cobradata_truth.txt",
                  result_files = "cobradata_results.txt", 
                  feature_id = "feature")
cobra <- COBRAData_from_text(truth_file = "cobradata_truth.txt", 
                             result_files = "cobradata_results.txt", 
                             feature_id = "feature")
cobra
